top.title: Not quite the same Bayern benchmark
top.description: Not quite the same Bayern benchmark Unfortunate in losing two talismans to injury, sling-wearing Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany had no experienced striker to call upon as his side tried to break down a dogged and determined 1. FC Köln in what would eventually end as a 1-1 stalemate on Friday night. Injuries to both Harry Kane and Michael Olise – in addition to Luis Díaz’s absence – exposed a glaring lack of depth at the business end of the pitch. Nathaniel Brown’s first-half equaliser came from nothing, while Lennart Karl and Tim Binder offered little of note throughout the second period. With the Ballon d'Or winner and a certain flying Frenchman nowhere in sight, proceedings at the Allianz Arena suddenly seemed a far cry from previous seasons. Dayot Upamecano’s reaction upon being replaced by Minjae Kim summed up the entire evening: one of clear, unadulterated frustration stemming in large part from a lack of rhythm or penetration. Credit has to go to the visitors for remaining steadfast in their efforts to earn something from this encounter. However, the second 45 minutes was crying out for a physical presence similar to that of Nicolas Jackson or the tenacity in close quarters of Raphaël Guerreiro. Despite enjoying more than two-thirds of the ball, Bayern registered a disappointing return of just two shots on target. Jamal Musiala, introduced with 20 minutes left to play, was largely ineffectual. With odds even in the closing stages, the expected flurry of corners and unrelenting pressure bearing down on the Südkurve failed to materialise. Leon Goretzka’s industrious nature, so often displayed even during the briefest of cameos, may have helped on that front. Naturally, an array of injuries to key personnel can decimate and eventually derail the best of sides. Calling on 19-year-old striker Noah Codjo-Evora with a matter of moments to go prompted a few raised eyebrows, while the sight of a previously exiled Sacha Boey on the bench serves as a constant reminder of pre-season transfer struggles. Fortunately, it was confirmed that Olise only suffered a bruised foot. On the other hand, Kane is set for his first significant spell on the sidelines since arriving in Munich after tearing an ankle ligament – the same injury recently suffered by Ismael Saibari. With the long-awaited return of Díaz next week, there will be an outlet on each flank but still a rather complex puzzle to solve down the middle.

top.title: Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar
top.description: Drivers were limited to 25 laps for each set of tyres in last year's Qatar Grand Prix [Getty Images] Formula 1 drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix. The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed Lusail track, which has a series of demanding, long-duration corners. It means teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix, as was the case last year. The limit applies on a single set of tyres whenever it is used across sessions. So mileage done in practice or qualifying, for example, would limit the number of laps that could be done on a set of tyres in the race. Pirelli said the limit was longer then last year's 25 laps because of the reduced downforce levels of the 2026 cars compared with 2025. "The increase has been made possible by the lower load levels recorded so far on the current generation of cars and by a further reinforcement of the tyre construction," a statement said. Last year, the limit led to a major strategic error by McLaren, who lost a win because they failed to pit under a safety car period when everyone else did. It is the third time in four years Pirelli has imposed a tyre-duration limit at Qatar, where running wide over flat kerbs in addition to the high-speed nature of the track is especially demanding for the tyres. Pirelli described the decision as a "precautionary measure" that was "linked to the unique characteristics of the Lusail circuit, which is particularly demanding in terms of energy loads, thermal stress and tread wear". In terms of the way the limit will be imposed, the statement said: "Laps will be counted cumulatively across all track sessions, including any laps completed under the safety car or virtual safety car. "As far as the grand prix is concerned, all laps completed from the start signal to the chequered flag will count towards the total. "Reconnaissance laps, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. "In all other track sessions, any lap that has been started but not completed will nevertheless be counted as a full lap. "Should a team assemble a tyre set using tyres that have covered different mileages, the tyre with the highest lap count will determine the mileage attributed to that set." top.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
top.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. 'Somebody has to stand up to that guy' - and Russell has his chance in Vegas Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. top.title: 'Somebody has to stand up to that guy' - and Russell has his chance in Vegas
top.description: Max Verstappen (left) and George Russell (right) will start on the front row in the Las Vegas Grand Prix [Getty Images] The Las Vegas Grand Prix will start with two drivers on the front row who dislike each other - and after qualifying one said of the other that "somebody has got to stand up to that guy". "That guy" is Max Verstappen, who starts his Red Bull from pole position. The driver criticising him is Mercedes' George Russell, who lines up second. Both were promoted after the fastest qualifier, new world champion Kimi Antonelli, was demoted by a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation for the season. Russell's beef stemmed from an incident in final practice, in which Verstappen overtook the Mercedes on the Las Vegas Strip, then veered in front of him into Turn 14. Russell, unhappy with the Dutchman's behaviour, dived down the Red Bull's inside on braking for the corner, got alongside, and then made his displeasure known by pushing Verstappen wide, the two cars making light contact. They were called to the stewards to discuss the incident. Verstappen was given a warning having been found to have made an "unpredictable change of direction under braking". After qualifying, Russell told Sky Italia: "I think the warning was fine. There's nothing in the rules to say that you cannot overtake someone who is starting their lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over. "He does this week in, week out, with many drivers. Everybody accepts it and I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." Russell's comments were not put to Verstappen as he had finished his media commitments by the time they emerged into wider knowledge in Las Vegas. Asked about the incident in the official news conference, Verstappen said: "Nothing happened." When Verstappen spoke to the Dutch media, he was again reluctant to be drawn on it. But asked whether it gave him extra motivation to beat Russell in the race, he said: "I don't need any extra motivation." George Russell and Max Verstappen battling for track position during final practice in Las Vegas [Getty Images] These two have history. This incident is almost exactly two years since they fell out in public following a row at the Qatar Grand Prix where Verstappen felt Russell had stepped over the line to get him a penalty that demoted him from pole position. They exchanged insults. Russell, in remarks that echo those from Las Vegas, said: "People have been bullied by Max for years now." Verstappen called Russell a "backstabber" and a "loser". top.description: Dripping Springs' Jacob Bremmer jumps to catch a touchdown pass above Judson's Myles Wisdom during the Class 6A Division II second round playoff game at Pieper's Warrior Coliseum on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Dripping Springs defeated Judson 59-28. Judson took the early lead in the first quarter before Dripping Springs took control behind running back Frank Accetta, who rushed for 209 yards and three touchdowns. The Tigers (10-1) take on Pharr-San Juan-Alamo North in the third round next week. Pharr-San Juan-Alamo North defeated Warren 46-15 in second-round action on Friday. "I don't think we did what we needed to do in all three phases. We just kept making mental mistake after mental mistake after mental mistake and whenever you're playing really good football teams, you can't beat good football teams playing that way." top.description: Giorgio Scalvini: Man United battling Liverpool, Chelsea for Atalanta defender Manchester United struggles at the back are likely to be addressed by INEOS in 2027, with fans already clamouring for defensive additions at the turn of the year. The Red Devils have let in 30 goals across competitions this season, including 19 in 10 games in the Premier League, where they have slipped to 18th in the table. The situation has prompted drastic actions from the club hierarchy – Michael Carrick has been removed from his position, while Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as his replacement. While there is optimism that the Argentine can pull the club out of dire straits, it is also evident that he will need backing in the transfer market to successfully implement his tactics. United need defensive reinforcements All signs indicate that defensive reinforcements will be at the centre of United’s transfer activity in 2027 and for good reason too. Harry Maguire is on the wrong side of 30 and out of contract at the end of this season. Lisandro Martínez has blown hot and cold this year, and will also enter the final six months of his contract in January. The Argentine remains linked with an exit at the turn of the year. The report acknowledges that there were concerns earlier this year whether the 22-year-old could return to his best after suffering an ACL injury in 2024 and spending considerable time on the sidelines with various knocks. top.title: ‘It’s a lie!’ – Mykhailo Mudryk hits back at Andriy Shevchenko as civil war erupts over banned substance suspension
top.description: Mykhailo Mudryk Chelsea 2026 - Getty Mykhailo Mudryk has sensationally accused Andriy Shevchenko of lying as the bitter dispute over the winger's doping ban escalates. The Tottenham Hotspur loanee claims he has firm evidence proving the Ukrainian Association of Football deliberately misled the investigation into his positive test. Mudryk brands Shevchenko a liar The bitter fallout surrounding Mudryk's lengthy suspension for a doping violation has taken an explosive turn. The Tottenham winger has publicly accused Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) president Shevchenko of lying. Mudryk, who is currently on a one-season loan from Chelsea, has been handed a suspension that runs from November 2024 to July 2026. The suspension was issued after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium. The forward firmly blames the UAF for his failed test and subsequent exile. He believes the prohibited substance entered his system while he was away on international duty with Ukraine. Shevchenko alleges false blame plot The war of words escalated dramatically following recent comments from Shevchenko . The former Chelsea and AC Milan striker alleged that Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked a UAF employee to falsely take the blame for the positive test. Shevchenko branded the winger's complaints as a "baseless slander against our people" and demanded a retraction. However, Mudryk fiercely hit back in a statement released on Friday to deny the claims. "Neither I nor my representatives made any such request," Mudryk declared, as quoted by BBC , categorically rejecting the accusation. Winger claims proof of cover-up Mudryk insists that the UAF actively attempted to mislead the investigation to distance the governing body from the scandal. He also accused the federation of being repeatedly slow to respond and deliberately withholding crucial documents from his lawyers. "My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible," Mudryk explained. "In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. One of those letters was leaked to the media by the UAF earlier today and clearly shows that my lawyers wanted 'true, verifiable and reliable information. "Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case. For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. That is, I have evidence to prove that their repeated assertions are wrong." top.title: Lens’ Robin Risser attracting Juventus and Inter interest, PL clubs also in hunt
top.description: Lens’ Robin Risser attracting Juventus and Inter interest, PL clubs also in hunt Lens keeper Robin Risser has had a significant rise to stardom in the last 12 months and has also managed to feature in the Champions League this season. As his stocks keep going up, interest in the Frenchman is only growing, with Inter, Juventus and several Premier League clubs in the hunt. Tuttomercatoweb provide details about the 21-year-old’s situation, reporting that the Nerazzurri have been following Risser for many months now. They’re unhappy with Josep Martinez’s form and could seek a replacement, which can turn out to be the Lens star himself. Milan have previously made contact for the keeper too but now, it is Juventus who are monitoring Risser closely. While they do have Guglielmo Vicario as the first-choice, the Lens man can become an option in the future. Most importantly, Risser is currently at the top of the Manchester City’s shortlist, with Gigio Donnarumma struggling. There is a chance even Liverpool could chose to invest in Risser, as competition from Bayern Munich also grows, with the Bavarians seeking to solve their keeper worries for the next ten years. For now, Lens’ price tag stands at €40 million, which could be complicated for Serie A clubs right now. But is clear the player has witnessed growth and a big move could soon be on the horizon. top.title: Real Madrid defender Eder Militao reveals what makes Jude Bellingham special: ‘Super competitive’
top.description: Real Madrid defender Eder Militao reveals what makes Jude Bellingham special: ‘Super competitive’ With all the internationals back in training, Real Madrid are set to take on Celta Vigo later today at the Santiago Bernabeu. Jose Mourinho has some big decisions to make ahead of kickoff, not only involving Vinicius Jr. and Yan Diomande but also involving internationals who played a hectic role in the recent hiatus. One such player is Jude Bellingham, who played a total of 173 minutes in two games during the recent international break. Militao praises Bellingham Real Madrid defender Eder Militao spoke to the media in a recent interview where he opened up on how Jude Bellingham is as a teammate behind the scenes. Quite unsurprisingly, he described the Englishman as a player who trains with the same intensity that he shows on the field. Militao is slowly returning. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) “Jude Bellingham? He’s super competitive, even in training,” he said, h/t Madrid Xtra . Elaborating on the monstrous mentality Bellingham has and how the dressing room mocks him for the same, Militao jovially said, “He hates losing. We always joke that he’s like an old man.” Elaborating on his recent interaction with the midfield star, Militao said, “I told Jude Bellingham, ‘Man, I’m so proud to have you on my team, seriously. You’re playing at an absolutely ridiculous level. It’s like you see the game in slow motion. “ Everything you do, even when someone tries to nick the ball off you, it’s like you’ve already spotted them six days beforehand.'” “He thanked me for my words. Jude likes Brazil. He’s always hanging out with us,” he added. Coming off a special hiatus Bellingham was electric against Spain. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Jude Bellingham was on duty with the English national team over the past few weeks and played a big part in his side’s two massive wins in the same period. Against Croatia, Bellingham assisted Morgan Rogers for the team’s opening goal in their 2-1 win. The bigger game notably came against Spain, and Bellingham was key in the result that saw Spain’s first defeat in over two years. On the night, he assisted one goal and ensured England’s attack stayed incisive enough to bypass the Spanish dominance.

top.title: Nick Bosa Given Candid Assessment of 49ers Future Amid Struggles
top.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Nick Bosa hasn’t been the dominant force the San Francisco 49ers need on their defensive line, particularly when it comes to pressuring opposing quarterbacks. Given his massive contract, questions are beginning to emerge about whether Bosa’s long-term future in San Francisco could be in doubt if his production doesn’t improve. This season so far, Bosa has played 172 total snaps on defense for the 49ers, leading to a 71.8 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran edge rusher has recorded 11 total pressures, zero sacks, 10 hurries, six stops, six solo tackles, and one QB hit. As a result, Mark Willard and Dan Dibley of 95.7 The Game shared their outlook on what the future holds for Bosa with the 49ers. “He’s not at a minimum right now, and very possibly, probably never again will he be who he used to be,” Willard said in a Nov. 19 video from 95.7 The Game. “Now, does that mean that he’s not potentially still rreally productive? “Put it this way: I don’t think the Niners are as far along as a lot of fans are with the idea that they’re trading or getting rid of Nick Bosa after this season. He is still their best pass rusher, and I don’t think it’s terribly close.” 49ers Better Off Reworking Nick Bosa’s Contract Meanwhile, Dibley believes that the Niners are better off reworking his deal rather than having to deal with the ramifications of having to cut ties with him. Moreover, Dibley notes that Bosa isn’t a bad player; he’s probably not worth what the 49ers are currently paying him. “When the cap hit is so unwieldy that you’re more likely to rework the deal to stretch him out and try to make it so that eventually, when you do want to move on from him, the cap hit will be less than about $45 million, which is what it would be if you went ahead and did that,” Dibley said. “He is still a serviceable pass rusher. If you think about what ACL recovery is like, the first year is not always roses and sunshine. Sometimes it takes time to get back.” Nick Bosa Is Having a Reality Check Moment Dibley notes that Bosa is currently dealing with what all players deal with as they approach their 30s, which is that what worked for them in their early to mid 20s to mid 20s isn’t working anymore. As a result, it’s on the 49ers’ edge rusher to adapt or get left behind. “Also, the idea of him coasting, I do think, is a bit of a reality check,” Dibley added. “You were elite, you’ve been elite all the way back to high school, and now you come back from your third ACL and think, well, I can still do A, B, and C. “You start to do it, and only four games in, you’re realizing that you’re not able to get around the corner like you used to [and] you can’t bend like you used to. Your jam, your shove, and all the rest of the things that have always worked aren’t working.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Nick Bosa Given Candid Assessment of 49ers Future Amid Struggles appeared first on HEAVY .

top.description: Toto Wolff believes George Russell was in the right position to claim pole when asked why Mercedes decided not to give the Briton a tow from Kimi Antonelli in Q3. nigeria.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
nigeria.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. nigeria.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
nigeria.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. nigeria.title: ‘Leadership should not depend on luck’ – Okoroama on preparing technical experts for management
nigeria.description: By Ayo Taiwo Nigerian engineering leader and business psychology specialist James Okoroama has introduced a leadership development model aimed at helping technically accomplished professionals navigate the challenges of transitioning into management. Okoroama presented his N-Curve Leadership Model at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Society for Maintenance & Reliability Professionals (SMRP), held in Raleigh, North Carolina, from September 28 to October 1. His presentation, titled “Leading Through the Dip: From Technical Expertise to Maintenance and Reliability Engineering Leadership Mastery,” examined why professionals who excel in technical roles sometimes struggle when promoted into leadership positions. The N-Curve model describes a transition in which employees may experience a temporary decline in confidence, effectiveness or perceived competence as they move from technical responsibilities to managing people and organisational performance. According to Okoroama, technical expertise does not automatically translate into the ability to lead teams, delegate responsibilities and develop other professionals. “We promote people for being the best fixer in the room, then ask them to stop fixing,” Okoroama said. “Of course there is a dip. The mistake is pretending it will not happen.” The model outlines a progression from technical mastery through promotion and a potential leadership dip, followed by adaptation and eventual leadership proficiency. Okoroama said that the transition requires professionals to move beyond individual technical achievements and develop skills in delegation, communication, coaching, conflict resolution and performance management. He introduced the model in a December 2025 research paper alongside a complementary framework known as the Situational Reliability Leadership Matrix, which proposes tailoring leadership development to individual readiness and organisational demands. His interest in the subject draws partly from his professional journey, which began with technical apprenticeship in Nigeria before progressing through equipment maintenance, reliability engineering, consulting and engineering management. He currently serves as a senior regional reliability engineering and robotics leader at Amazon, where he leads a technical organisation of more than 600 professionals supporting industrial automation and robotics operations. In 2026, he also serves as an RME Engagement and Workforce Development Strategy Partner within Amazon’s North America Customer Fulfillment network. Okoroama holds a Master of Science degree from the University of South Wales, where his studies explored the relationship between human behaviour, organisational performance and leadership. nigeria.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
nigeria.description: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.” Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.” AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.” Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.” Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them. A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes. nigeria.title: Why obesity hits men harder than women – Study
nigeria.description: By Shola Ogundipe Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women. The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently beneath the skin, with immune cells living inside body fat either helping to protect against inflammation and metabolic disorders or making them worse, depending on biological sex. Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, US, found that a group of immune cells known as eosinophils, traditionally associated with allergies and asthma, perform different functions in the fat tissue of male and female mice. While certain populations of these cells appear to protect against obesity-related inflammation, others may contribute to harmful metabolic changes. The study, titled “Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity”, was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine. The findings, published in the journal PNAS Nexus, challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar in structure and function. They also raise questions about whether obesity treatments targeting the immune system should be designed differently for men and women. Led by biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik, the study used high-resolution single-cell sequencing to examine how individual immune cells behave in fat tissue. What emerged was an unexpected picture. The researchers identified six distinct populations of eosinophils in adipose tissue, each with its own genetic activity and potentially different biological functions. The discovery suggests that these cells are not simply passive occupants of body fat. Some may help maintain metabolic health, while others may contribute to the inflammatory processes associated with obesity. “Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought,” said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences at UCR’s School of Medicine. She explained that identifying and activating the biological pathways responsible for producing protective eosinophils could open new possibilities for improving metabolic health. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. sports.title: Not quite the same Bayern benchmark
sports.description: Not quite the same Bayern benchmark Unfortunate in losing two talismans to injury, sling-wearing Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany had no experienced striker to call upon as his side tried to break down a dogged and determined 1. FC Köln in what would eventually end as a 1-1 stalemate on Friday night. Injuries to both Harry Kane and Michael Olise – in addition to Luis Díaz’s absence – exposed a glaring lack of depth at the business end of the pitch. Nathaniel Brown’s first-half equaliser came from nothing, while Lennart Karl and Tim Binder offered little of note throughout the second period. With the Ballon d'Or winner and a certain flying Frenchman nowhere in sight, proceedings at the Allianz Arena suddenly seemed a far cry from previous seasons. Dayot Upamecano’s reaction upon being replaced by Minjae Kim summed up the entire evening: one of clear, unadulterated frustration stemming in large part from a lack of rhythm or penetration. Credit has to go to the visitors for remaining steadfast in their efforts to earn something from this encounter. However, the second 45 minutes was crying out for a physical presence similar to that of Nicolas Jackson or the tenacity in close quarters of Raphaël Guerreiro. Despite enjoying more than two-thirds of the ball, Bayern registered a disappointing return of just two shots on target. Jamal Musiala, introduced with 20 minutes left to play, was largely ineffectual. With odds even in the closing stages, the expected flurry of corners and unrelenting pressure bearing down on the Südkurve failed to materialise. Leon Goretzka’s industrious nature, so often displayed even during the briefest of cameos, may have helped on that front. Naturally, an array of injuries to key personnel can decimate and eventually derail the best of sides. Calling on 19-year-old striker Noah Codjo-Evora with a matter of moments to go prompted a few raised eyebrows, while the sight of a previously exiled Sacha Boey on the bench serves as a constant reminder of pre-season transfer struggles. Fortunately, it was confirmed that Olise only suffered a bruised foot. On the other hand, Kane is set for his first significant spell on the sidelines since arriving in Munich after tearing an ankle ligament – the same injury recently suffered by Ismael Saibari. With the long-awaited return of Díaz next week, there will be an outlet on each flank but still a rather complex puzzle to solve down the middle.

sports.title: Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar
sports.description: Drivers were limited to 25 laps for each set of tyres in last year's Qatar Grand Prix [Getty Images] Formula 1 drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix. The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed Lusail track, which has a series of demanding, long-duration corners. It means teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix, as was the case last year. The limit applies on a single set of tyres whenever it is used across sessions. So mileage done in practice or qualifying, for example, would limit the number of laps that could be done on a set of tyres in the race. Pirelli said the limit was longer then last year's 25 laps because of the reduced downforce levels of the 2026 cars compared with 2025. "The increase has been made possible by the lower load levels recorded so far on the current generation of cars and by a further reinforcement of the tyre construction," a statement said. Last year, the limit led to a major strategic error by McLaren, who lost a win because they failed to pit under a safety car period when everyone else did. It is the third time in four years Pirelli has imposed a tyre-duration limit at Qatar, where running wide over flat kerbs in addition to the high-speed nature of the track is especially demanding for the tyres. Pirelli described the decision as a "precautionary measure" that was "linked to the unique characteristics of the Lusail circuit, which is particularly demanding in terms of energy loads, thermal stress and tread wear". In terms of the way the limit will be imposed, the statement said: "Laps will be counted cumulatively across all track sessions, including any laps completed under the safety car or virtual safety car. "As far as the grand prix is concerned, all laps completed from the start signal to the chequered flag will count towards the total. "Reconnaissance laps, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. "In all other track sessions, any lap that has been started but not completed will nevertheless be counted as a full lap. "Should a team assemble a tyre set using tyres that have covered different mileages, the tyre with the highest lap count will determine the mileage attributed to that set." sports.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. sports.description: Max Verstappen (left) and George Russell (right) will start on the front row in the Las Vegas Grand Prix [Getty Images] The Las Vegas Grand Prix will start with two drivers on the front row who dislike each other - and after qualifying one said of the other that "somebody has got to stand up to that guy". "That guy" is Max Verstappen, who starts his Red Bull from pole position. The driver criticising him is Mercedes' George Russell, who lines up second. Both were promoted after the fastest qualifier, new world champion Kimi Antonelli, was demoted by a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation for the season. Russell's beef stemmed from an incident in final practice, in which Verstappen overtook the Mercedes on the Las Vegas Strip, then veered in front of him into Turn 14. Russell, unhappy with the Dutchman's behaviour, dived down the Red Bull's inside on braking for the corner, got alongside, and then made his displeasure known by pushing Verstappen wide, the two cars making light contact. They were called to the stewards to discuss the incident. Verstappen was given a warning having been found to have made an "unpredictable change of direction under braking". After qualifying, Russell told Sky Italia: "I think the warning was fine. There's nothing in the rules to say that you cannot overtake someone who is starting their lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over. "He does this week in, week out, with many drivers. Everybody accepts it and I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." Russell's comments were not put to Verstappen as he had finished his media commitments by the time they emerged into wider knowledge in Las Vegas. Asked about the incident in the official news conference, Verstappen said: "Nothing happened." When Verstappen spoke to the Dutch media, he was again reluctant to be drawn on it. But asked whether it gave him extra motivation to beat Russell in the race, he said: "I don't need any extra motivation." sports.description: Mykhailo Mudryk Chelsea 2026 - Getty Mykhailo Mudryk has sensationally accused Andriy Shevchenko of lying as the bitter dispute over the winger's doping ban escalates. The Tottenham Hotspur loanee claims he has firm evidence proving the Ukrainian Association of Football deliberately misled the investigation into his positive test. Mudryk brands Shevchenko a liar The bitter fallout surrounding Mudryk's lengthy suspension for a doping violation has taken an explosive turn. The Tottenham winger has publicly accused Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) president Shevchenko of lying. Mudryk, who is currently on a one-season loan from Chelsea, has been handed a suspension that runs from November 2024 to July 2026. The suspension was issued after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium. The forward firmly blames the UAF for his failed test and subsequent exile. He believes the prohibited substance entered his system while he was away on international duty with Ukraine. Shevchenko alleges false blame plot The war of words escalated dramatically following recent comments from Shevchenko . The former Chelsea and AC Milan striker alleged that Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked a UAF employee to falsely take the blame for the positive test. Shevchenko branded the winger's complaints as a "baseless slander against our people" and demanded a retraction. However, Mudryk fiercely hit back in a statement released on Friday to deny the claims. "Neither I nor my representatives made any such request," Mudryk declared, as quoted by BBC , categorically rejecting the accusation. Winger claims proof of cover-up Mudryk insists that the UAF actively attempted to mislead the investigation to distance the governing body from the scandal. He also accused the federation of being repeatedly slow to respond and deliberately withholding crucial documents from his lawyers. "My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible," Mudryk explained. "In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. "Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case. For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. sports.title: Nick Bosa Given Candid Assessment of 49ers Future Amid Struggles
sports.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Nick Bosa hasn’t been the dominant force the San Francisco 49ers need on their defensive line, particularly when it comes to pressuring opposing quarterbacks. Given his massive contract, questions are beginning to emerge about whether Bosa’s long-term future in San Francisco could be in doubt if his production doesn’t improve. This season so far, Bosa has played 172 total snaps on defense for the 49ers, leading to a 71.8 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran edge rusher has recorded 11 total pressures, zero sacks, 10 hurries, six stops, six solo tackles, and one QB hit. As a result, Mark Willard and Dan Dibley of 95.7 The Game shared their outlook on what the future holds for Bosa with the 49ers. “He’s not at a minimum right now, and very possibly, probably never again will he be who he used to be,” Willard said in a Nov. 19 video from 95.7 The Game. “Now, does that mean that he’s not potentially still rreally productive? “Put it this way: I don’t think the Niners are as far along as a lot of fans are with the idea that they’re trading or getting rid of Nick Bosa after this season. He is still their best pass rusher, and I don’t think it’s terribly close.” 49ers Better Off Reworking Nick Bosa’s Contract Meanwhile, Dibley believes that the Niners are better off reworking his deal rather than having to deal with the ramifications of having to cut ties with him. Moreover, Dibley notes that Bosa isn’t a bad player; he’s probably not worth what the 49ers are currently paying him. “When the cap hit is so unwieldy that you’re more likely to rework the deal to stretch him out and try to make it so that eventually, when you do want to move on from him, the cap hit will be less than about $45 million, which is what it would be if you went ahead and did that,” Dibley said. “He is still a serviceable pass rusher. If you think about what ACL recovery is like, the first year is not always roses and sunshine. Sometimes it takes time to get back.” Nick Bosa Is Having a Reality Check Moment Dibley notes that Bosa is currently dealing with what all players deal with as they approach their 30s, which is that what worked for them in their early to mid 20s to mid 20s isn’t working anymore. As a result, it’s on the 49ers’ edge rusher to adapt or get left behind. “Also, the idea of him coasting, I do think, is a bit of a reality check,” Dibley added. “You were elite, you’ve been elite all the way back to high school, and now you come back from your third ACL and think, well, I can still do A, B, and C. “You start to do it, and only four games in, you’re realizing that you’re not able to get around the corner like you used to [and] you can’t bend like you used to. Your jam, your shove, and all the rest of the things that have always worked aren’t working.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Nick Bosa Given Candid Assessment of 49ers Future Amid Struggles appeared first on HEAVY .

sports.description: Toto Wolff believes George Russell was in the right position to claim pole when asked why Mercedes decided not to give the Briton a tow from Kimi Antonelli in Q3. Over the course of the session, Russell asked whether he could receive a tow from his teammate Antonelli, considering that the Italian has a five-place grid penalty for tomorrow's race. However, Mercedes did not arrange that for him. Antonelli was the last to start his lap and, after receiving a good tow from Racing Bulls, set the fastest time in Q3. Speaking to Sky Sports, Mercedes team principal Wolff said: "Actually, George, for me, had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front. We need to find out because I think there was some kind of… Turns 7-8-9, whether that was a mistake or something else happened, we need to… I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap, because he was quickest all the time." sports.title: ‘He Let Everybody Know He Has Beef With Joe Buck’ — Former Eagles All-Pro Understands Why Troy Aikman Went Scorched Earth
sports.description: Aug 5, 2023; Canton, OH, USA; Troy Aikman arrives on the red carpet for the 2023 Pro Football Hall of Fame Enshrinement at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium. © Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports We’re past the halfway mark of the season, and while there’s been a lot of action on the field, some animosity in the broadcasting game has also been drawing attention. We’re, of course, talking about Troy Aikman’s beef with his Monday Night Football colleague, Joe Buck. Amid reports that the two had a verbal altercation ahead of Week 5’s primetime Los Angeles Rams-Buffalo Bills game, Aikman decided to kinda-sorta pour jet fuel on the fire this week during an appearance on 96.7 The Ticket, when he said, “Joe’s always wanted a one-man booth.” While that was a light-hearted throwaway line, the damage was already done, as their beef spilled out of the broadcast booth and onto the radio. Hugh Douglas came away impressed by the way Aikman did it. Hugh Douglas, the former Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro defensive end, made it clear he was impressed by how Aikman went about it all. Why Hugh Douglas Called Troy Aikman’s Move ‘Gangster’ At first, Douglas said he heard the clip as Aikman airing a grievance while his broadcast partner tried to smooth it over. “I heard the snippet and I was like, wow, he took that beef to the radio and Joe Buck was trying to, you know, calm it down,” Douglas said on 94WIP . His view changed when he was told that Buck had not been on the air with Aikman at all. “But when you told me he wasn’t even there, I’m like, that was kind of gangster of Troy.” What stood out to Douglas was that Aikman made no attempt to keep the dispute private. “He let everybody know that he has beef with Joe Buck,” Douglas said, adding that Aikman’s message amounted to “Hey, yeah, we got beef.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Douglas also questioned whether Buck would take the fight, so to speak, to Aikman, wondering aloud, “Is Joe Buck about that life? That’s what we’re talking about.” Can Buck and Aikman Last the Season? Then the talk turned to what comes next. Douglas was asked whether the pair can stay together through the rest of the regular season, at least one playoff game, and the Super Bowl. Super Bowl LXI is mere months away, and the timing of Aikman’s comments could not have been worse. Just days earlier, ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said that he was “disappointed” by how the media was reporting on the tension between the two veteran broadcasters. Pitaro recruited the pair from Fox, where Buck and Aikman called six Super Bowls over a two-decade stint at the network. Per The Athletic, ESPN and Buck agreed to a new six-year, $108 million deal, a roughly 20% increase over his previous contract. Aikman, meanwhile, does not have a new deal in place, a development that has been reported to be at the center of the tension between the two. sports.title: 'Making my job easier': CSK head coach Zaheer Khan breaks silence on MS Dhoni's 'unexpected' retirement
sports.description: Chennai Super Kings head coach Zaheer Khan has admitted that MS Dhoni's decision to retire from playing in the Indian Premier League came as a surprise to him, while describing the end of the former captain's playing career as an emotional moment for the franchise. Dhoni will no longer take the field for CSK but will remain associated with the five-time champions as their team mentor from IPL 2027. Zaheer said the team would miss having Dhoni as a player but was looking forward to working with him in his new role. "It's been an emotional week for all of us, with mixed feelings. Every year, you're hoping that MS is going to be seen playing a role for the team this season. He will be, but in a different avatar, and hence the mixed feelings. "I think the journey he has had in cricket has been amazing. Srinivasan rightly said that there is no CSK without MS, and that surely is the case," Zaheer said in a video uploaded on CSK's YouTube channel. Dhoni's retirement from playing was confirmed on November 17, when CSK announced that he would take up the role of team mentor. Zaheer said he was also looking forward to having Dhoni's experience and guidance as he takes charge of the team ahead of the next season. "It's mixed feelings for me personally because you're not going to see him as part of the playing team. But I'm excited that he's going to be sharing the burden with me, making my job easier, guiding us in the right direction and being a mentor to us. "So, yeah, excited about that, looking ahead, but also emotional about the decision he has taken," Zaheer added. Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 crowns. However, he did not play a single match during the 2026 season because of fitness concerns. While CSK owner Rupa Gurunath had earlier revealed that Dhoni had indicated he might not return as a player, Zaheer said he had not seriously considered the possibility. His focus, he explained, had been on preparing the squad and planning for the upcoming season. "Not at all. I think, for a couple of reasons, it was the last year of this cycle. So maybe, looking ahead at a fresh cycle, those kind of thoughts would have popped into my head," Zaheer said. "But right now, I wasn't even thinking about it. Obviously, you're looking at the season, you're looking at the stack-up of your team, the playing XI. I haven't personally given it a thought because, you know, it's MS. He knows what is the right thing to do and when is the time to act upon a certain thing. "So I was not really spending my time and energy going in that direction. Whatever it is, it's going to be his decision. I'm planning for the season. "So, yes, it was unexpected for me personally when he did mention it in a very, very subtle way, as you know, he doesn't like to create massive news out of it. It just was in the discussion, casually mentioning that, okay, this is it, you're going to have some extra money to go into the auction with," Zaheer added.

technology.title: NASA Mars rover and orbiter suffer glitches
technology.description: It's been a bad few weeks for technology on and off the planet, as NASA reported problems with its Perseverance Mars rover and Odyssey orbiter this week. For Perseverance, the problem seems to be a relatively straightforward communications issue that has paused science operations because of low data rates. The Odyssey orbiter, however, is facing an issue that could end the mission. The 2001 Mars Odyssey reached orbit around Mars in October 2001 to search for evidence of water and ice on the surface. The mission was supposed to last two and a half years, but the spacecraft's operations have been extended for a quarter of a century. In that time, it has had its fair share of ups and downs, including the failure of one of its four reaction wheels in 2013. Three reaction wheels are needed to orient the spacecraft; otherwise, it must fall back to its hydrazine thrusters. Earlier in November, between the 4th and 6th, Odyssey dropped into safe mode, which engineers determined was caused by one of the remaining reaction wheels stopping spinning. Science data stopped flowing as the team worked to recover the component; the good news was that the wheel moved when commanded. The bad news is that if the thrusters need to be used, only a few months of fuel remain. More bad news is that the spacecraft is part of NASA's Mars Relay Network, and was responsible for sending back the first post-landing images from the Phoenix lander and the Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity rovers. Its loss (should it come to that) would therefore be keenly felt. In the event the orbiter is indeed approaching the end of the road, the European Space Agency's Mars Express (MEX) and Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) could pick up some of the load although, as a former ESA insider put it: "MEX is a science mission that can do relay where TGO is a relay mission that also does science." According to NASA, TGO already sends the most relay data from Mars to Earth. The challenge facing the Perseverance trundlebot is one of communication. On October 30, the rover's main computer detected problems with the primary radio (a series of "heartbeats" from the device did not arrive as expected) and automatically switched to a redundant backup, placing itself in a protective safe mode. So far, so expected. Engineers brought the rover back from safe mode, analyzed the data, and made an unpleasant discovery. The backup radio was not performing as it should – it was operating at approximately half of its expected power output. Both radios were therefore deemed inoperable – at least until the team has got to the bottom of the issues – and the rover has used X-band communications over its high-gain antenna to talk to Earth ever since. The problem here is that the connection provides a significantly lower data rate, meaning science and instrument operations are on hold. Engineers are working first to return the backup radio to operational status, then to address the primary. ®

technology.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
technology.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. technology.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
technology.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. technology.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
technology.description: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access.
